findings.issue_text: Removal of per-user canView filter in searchForUser (UsersResource.java ~455) exposes full user list to admins with only query-users permission, a privilege escalation/data exposure
Dropping the per-user canView filter silently excludes users granted direct fine-grained VIEW/MANAGE Users-resource permissions (not group-based) from all admin user searches
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() global override returns true when caller holds only the VIEW scope, allowing view-only admins to create groups via requireManage()
V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission dropped the canManage() short-circuit, so manage-only admins get ambiguous empty-set sentinel behavior and intermittent wrong search results

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs; non-matching resource ids cause users in those groups to silently vanish from search results
BruteForceUsersResource (~147) has same unfiltered-search exposure: admin without view permission or group grants gets all realm users returned in brute-force listing

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 56) accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient for realm-wide group management, letting a view-only admin create, update, and delete groups — privilege escalation; scope list should be {MANAGE} only

UsersResource.searchForUser (~line 445) and BruteForceUsersResource (~line 147) removed the defensive post-filter .filter(usersEvaluator::canView), so admins with no view-users/manage-users role but only group-level view scope get unrestricted search results, exposing every user in the realm (user enumeration/info disclosure)

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (~line 110) collects authorization-resource UUIDs instead of Keycloak group IDs (group ID is stored as the resource name), so the returned set never matches real groups and group-scoped user searches/counts silently return nothing

hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by name = resource-ID, so per-group VIEW_MEMBER permissions are ignored and results become all-or-nothing based on the all-groups resource

AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (~line 105) now throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types instead of falling back to the previous type-level resource resolution, breaking extensions relying on custom resource types

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs an unbounded resource scan with per-resource policy evaluation (N+1): iterates every group via resourceStore.findByType and calls hasPermission per group (resourceStore.findByName, policyStore.findByResource, evaluatePermission), materialized into a HashSet on every user search/count request by non-global-view admins; no caching, pagination, or early exit

canView(GroupModel) in GroupPermissionsV2 (~48-56) removes the canViewGlobal short-circuit, causing every group in the stream in GroupsResource.java:112 and GroupResource.java:177 to be permission-evaluated via hasPermission with no memoization; in GroupResource.getSubGroups the subgroup stream is fetched unbounded (-1, -1) and the filter runs before paginatedStream, so all subgroups are evaluated even when only max (default 10) are returned

hasPermission fallback path (~150-170) makes redundant store round-trips on every denied check: falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource and policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() — an extra two store round-trips plus evaluation-context setup per denied group, amplifying issue #2

GroupResource.getSubGroupsStream (174-181) fetches all matching subgroups unbounded (-1, -1) before client-side permission filtering and pagination, causing under-filled/empty pages and evaluating every subgroup per page request

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission result is not cached per request/session (GroupPermissions.java:298+ / GroupPermissionsV2.java:104), unlike MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() which caches its evaluator; a single admin UI page load calls both UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount, doubling the full realm group scan and per-group policy evaluation

Correctness concern: removal of the per-user .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) in UsersResource.searchForUser means user results are governed solely by the GROUPS attribute filter — the group-id set built from VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS resources won't reflect VIEW/MANAGE scoped group resources, and direct user-level grants are silently dropped from search results for restricted admins

Removal of post-search canView filter in UsersResource.java:445–452 (searchForUser) means callers lacking users().canView() with empty groupIds trigger unrestricted searchForUserStream, returning every user in the realm to an unauthorized admin at GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users; same latent exposure in BruteForceUsersResource.java:147–153

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 46–53) grants manage permission from the VIEW scope via hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), violating the documented MANAGE-only contract on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() and enabling privilege escalation on group create/update/delete paths

Breaking public SPI/interface surface: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) deleted from the interface and its impl removed from GroupPermissions.java:298–311, with getGroupsWithViewPermission() renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()
Breaking public API: UserPermissions public canManageDefault() and canViewDefault() methods deleted (also removed from RolePermissions.canMapRole call site, confirming external usage existed)

Breaking public API: ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...) deleted, a public static utility in server-spi-private used by extensions, with no deprecation cycle and binary compatibility breaks (NoSuchMethodError)

V2 GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds the authorization resource's ID (groupResource.getId()) to the granted set, but hasPermission looks resources up by name; unless resources are created with id == groupId, the UserModel.GROUPS attribute contains resource UUIDs instead of group IDs so the user-search store filter matches nothing and group-scoped admins see no users

Scope drift between canView(group) (satisfied by VIEW/MANAGE scopes) and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (collects only VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS), so an admin granted view on a group sees the group resource but its member users don't appear in user search results

getOrCreateResource in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (~105–112) now throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types where it previously fell through with null name and hit null-handling, causing 500s for callers/extensions passing custom or future resource types

AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:71–98) moved the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check from inside the listener to around manager.register(...), so a listener registered while the feature was off never cleans up group resources when the feature is later enabled, leaving stale permission resources

Removed per-user canView filter in UsersResource.searchForUser combined with getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning an empty set in both 'global view' and 'no view permission' cases, so the GROUPS session attribute is never set and searchForUserStream runs unrestricted, leaking the full user list to admins with zero view permissions

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as satisfying manage (falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), granting write/manage access to admins with only read-only view grants — privilege escalation

registerListener ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved from per-event to registration time; if Profile is not yet resolved during early bootstrap the cleanup listener is never registered, leaking stale group/role permission resources

Removal of canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupResource and GroupsResource causes full per-group policy evaluation for every group in the stream even for admins with global view, turning O(1) into O(n) authz evaluations — performance regression

GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes while canView(group) accepts VIEW/MANAGE, causing inconsistent results: admins granted VIEW can open a group page but user searches scoped by GROUPS return no members, and counts disagree across endpoints
ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse can NPE on 201 responses without a Location header (or when assertion framework continues on failure), producing a less diagnosable error in test infrastructure

Removal of defensive in-stream permission filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource.java:455 and BruteForceUsersResource.java:~147 is untested; if a user federation/provider ignores the GROUPS session attribute, a group-scoped admin silently sees all users

V1 semantics change in GroupPermissions.java:298 — guard now checks only canView() instead of canView() || canManage(), so admins with MANAGE_USERS but not VIEW_USERS now get a non-empty group set; no V1 test covers this
AdminPermissions.java:74 — ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved to registration time, so listener is never registered if the feature is toggled on after registration; untested
GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest leaks user policies — same policy name 'Only My Admin User Policy' reused across multiple tests without cleanup, causing collisions or order-dependent results
No test for GroupResource.java:177 getSubGroups pagination-with-filter interaction — filtering before pagination can return fewer-than-max results for scoped admins
BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 group-scoped brute-force user search is completely untested, duplicating UsersResource logic and prone to drift
GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:52 contains a double semicolon typo (new GroupRepresentation();;)
MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope and canManageMembership path added to schema have no test coverage at all

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 46) global check falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing callers with only the view scope on all-groups to manage groups — a security leak and inconsistent with the per-resource canManage(group) which checks only MANAGE

Inconsistent resource identity in GroupPermissionsV2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects groupResource.getId() while hasPermission(groupId, ...) resolves via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId); if resource IDs differ from group IDs, the returned set is not usable group IDs for UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource consumers

LSP violation: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides 8 methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException; the GroupPermissionManagement surface should be split from the evaluator interface instead of stubbed

Duplicated getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() logic across GroupPermissions.java and GroupPermissionsV2.java (~20-line near-identical implementations differing only in the permission-evaluation predicate); extract the skeleton into the base class with a hook

Widened visibility (private → protected) of root, resourceStore, policyStore fields in GroupPermissions.java:56-58 purely for subclass access, leaking store internals instead of exposing protected behavior hooks

resolveGroup in AdminPermissionsSchema.java:181-186 breaks the naming contract of resolveUser/resolveClient by returning group.getId() (an ID) where siblings return human-meaningful names; rename or document the divergence

Duplicated 'GROUPS session attribute' pre-search logic: UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser contain byte-for-byte identical blocks (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission → setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) → toRepresentation); should live in one shared helper

Authorization filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` silently removed from UsersResource.searchForUser; admins with QUERY_USERS but no VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS role and empty groupIds get no GROUPS attribute set, so search returns every user in the realm
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly passes when admin has only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() and create/update groups

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds authz resource IDs instead of group IDs (group ID is stored as resource name), causing user search/count to silently return zero users for admins with legitimate VIEW_MEMBERS permissions
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only scans per-group resources and ignores grants on the typed all-groups resource, inconsistent with canViewMembers(group) which honors the all-groups fallback

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission creates persisted authorization resources on read paths via getOrCreateResource, causing read-only requests to mutate state and risking ModelDuplicateException races on concurrent first requests

Feature-gate check for ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ moved from per-event evaluation in onEvent to registration time, so enabling the feature after startup leaves the cleanup listener unregistered and orphaned authz resources accumulate

Removal of canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupResource.getSubGroups and GroupsResource.getGroups causes a per-group permission evaluation on every listing, a performance regression for admins with global view rights

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

This mismatch breaks group-scoped queries (users search/count) because returned IDs don’t match actual group IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of per-user canView filter in searchForUser (UsersResource.java ~455) exposes full user list to admins with only query-users permission, a privilege escalation/data exposure

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser, the diff removes `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from the user search stream and now directly passes `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction added here is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. For a caller who can pass the query endpoint (e.g., has QUERY_USERS) but does not have global view/manage and has no group-based view-members permissions, `groupIds` will be empty, no session attribute is set, and the removed per-user `canView` filter no longer prevents returning users. This creates a verifiable data exposure/privilege escalation risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropping the per-user canView filter silently excludes users granted direct fine-grained VIEW/MANAGE Users-resource permissions (not group-based) from all admin user searches

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the change removes `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)`. Removing a filter cannot by itself *exclude* users that were previously included (it would tend to include more results, potentially including unauthorized users, depending on downstream logic). Also, the group-based session restriction (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)`) was already used before (when `!auth.users().canView()`), and is still only set when the returned set is non-empty; this diff does not show any new logic that would specifically hide users with direct fine-grained user permissions. The finding’s stated exclusion mechanism is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() global override returns true when caller holds only the VIEW scope, allowing view-only admins to create groups via requireManage()
V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission dropped the canManage() short-circuit, so manage-only admins get ambiguous empty-set sentinel behavior and intermittent wrong search results

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` now short-circuits only on `root.users().canView()` (previously `canView() || canManage()`). But `UserPermissions.canView()` already returns true for manage-capable admins because it checks `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` and also treats `MANAGE` permission as sufficient (`hasPermission(..., VIEW, MANAGE)`). So a “manage-only admin” would still hit the `canView()` short-circuit and get the empty-set sentinel; dropping the explicit `canManage()` check is redundant rather than behavior-changing. The claimed “intermittent wrong search results” is also not evidenced by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects authorization resource IDs instead of group model IDs; non-matching resource ids cause users in those groups to silently vanish from search results
BruteForceUsersResource (~147) has same unfiltered-search exposure: admin without view permission or group grants gets all realm users returned in brute-force listing

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not verifiably introduce (or newly expose) an “unfiltered search” in BruteForceUsersResource. That method already called `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` without an explicit `usersEvaluator::canView` filter before the change, and it still does after. The only behavioral change shown is switching from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and removing the surrounding `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard; neither change, on its face, demonstrates that an admin with no view permission and no group grants will now receive all users. Whether results are restricted when `UserModel.GROUPS` is absent depends on `searchForUserStream`/`toRepresentation` behavior, which is not shown in the diff, so the claimed exposure cannot be confirmed from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 56) accepts the VIEW scope as sufficient for realm-wide group management, letting a view-only admin create, update, and delete groups — privilege escalation; scope list should be {MANAGE} only

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, if the caller lacks `MANAGE_USERS`, it returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e., realm-wide *VIEW* on the Groups resource type is treated as sufficient for `canManage()`. Given `canManage()` is the realm-level manage check (used when there is no specific `GroupModel`, e.g., create/top-level operations), this makes a view-only scope satisfy a manage gate, which is a privilege escalation risk. The helper `hasPermission(...)` explicitly returns true if any evaluated permission contains one of the expected scopes, so VIEW alone would pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser (~line 445) and BruteForceUsersResource (~line 147) removed the defensive post-filter .filter(usersEvaluator::canView), so admins with no view-users/manage-users role but only group-level view scope get unrestricted search results, exposing every user in the realm (user enumeration/info disclosure)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show removal of the explicit post-filtering step `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser` and analogous logic in `BruteForceUsersResource`, now relying on setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (from `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`) to constrain results. However, the claim that this *necessarily* yields unrestricted results/user enumeration cannot be verified from the diff alone because the enforcement behavior of `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` with/without the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute is not shown. What is verifiable is that a defense-in-depth authorization check was removed and correctness now depends on lower-layer behavior, which is a concrete review concern but not a proven defect from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (~line 110) collects authorization-resource UUIDs instead of Keycloak group IDs (group ID is stored as the resource name), so the returned set never matches real groups and group-scoped user searches/counts silently return nothing
matched_golden_ids: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is returning authorization resource UUIDs (resource.getId()) while permission evaluation and downstream filtering/counting expect real Keycloak group IDs (stored as the resource name). This mismatch breaks group-scoped queries (users search/count) because returned IDs don’t match actual group IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up resources by name = resource-ID, so per-group VIEW_MEMBER permissions are ignored and results become all-or-nothing based on the all-groups resource

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> { if (hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)) ... }). But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), i.e., it expects a *resource name* (here intended to be the groupId used as resource name elsewhere, e.g. tests create permissions using group.getId()). Passing groupResource.getId() (the authorization Resource internal ID) will typically not match findByName, causing resource==null and the method to fall back to evaluating the GROUPS resource-type (“all-groups”) resource. That means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are skipped/ignored and the result becomes dependent on whether an all-groups permission exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (~line 105) now throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types instead of falling back to the previous type-level resource resolution, breaking extensions relying on custom resource types

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, the diff replaces an if/else chain with a switch that has a `default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Resource type [" + resourceType + "] not found.")`. This is a concrete behavior change: any caller passing a resourceType other than the schema’s known constants (Clients/Groups/Users) will now fail immediately. The claim about a prior “fallback to type-level resource resolution” is not verifiable from the shown diff (the rest of the method isn’t included), but the new hard-fail on unknown types is real and could be an SPI/API compatibility concern for extensions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs an unbounded resource scan with per-resource policy evaluation (N+1): iterates every group via resourceStore.findByType and calls hasPermission per group (resourceStore.findByName, policyStore.findByResource, evaluatePermission), materialized into a HashSet on every user search/count request by non-global-view admins; no caching, pagination, or early exit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` which iterates all group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and, for each, calls `hasPermission(...)` that performs additional lookups (`resourceStore.findByName`, `policyStore.findByResource`) and permission evaluation (`root.evaluatePermission(...)`). The method materializes results into a new `HashSet` each call. The diff also changes user search/count paths to call this set-building method (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount(...)` and `searchForUser(...)`, and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)` now use `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`), making this potentially an unbounded per-request scan/evaluation for non-global-view admins. This is a concrete performance/architecture issue introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canView(GroupModel) in GroupPermissionsV2 (~48-56) removes the canViewGlobal short-circuit, causing every group in the stream in GroupsResource.java:112 and GroupResource.java:177 to be permission-evaluated via hasPermission with no memoization; in GroupResource.getSubGroups the subgroup stream is fetched unbounded (-1, -1) and the filter runs before paginatedStream, so all subgroups are evaluated even when only max (default 10) are returned

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous `canViewGlobal` short-circuit in both `GroupsResource#getGroups` (now `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`) and `GroupResource#getSubGroups` (now `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)`), meaning `canView(GroupModel)` is invoked per element rather than allowing a single global check to bypass per-group evaluation. In `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canView(GroupModel)` performs `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`, which calls `root.evaluatePermission(...)` and does not memoize results, so this can increase evaluation cost across large streams. Also, `GroupResource#getSubGroups` still fetches subgroups with `-1, -1` and applies the permission filter before `paginatedStream(...)`, so many subgroups may be evaluated even if only `max` (default 10) are ultimately returned. This is a performance/scalability concern grounded in the diff, not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission fallback path (~150-170) makes redundant store round-trips on every denied check: falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource and policyStore.findByResource(...).isEmpty() — an extra two store round-trips plus evaluation-context setup per denied group, amplifying issue #2

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, when a group-specific `Resource` is not found (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null), it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` and then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` before evaluating permissions. This introduces extra store lookups on that fallback path, which can occur repeatedly for denied checks across many groups, making the performance concern diff-grounded. It’s not a correctness defect per se, but a concrete efficiency/architecture issue created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResource.getSubGroupsStream (174-181) fetches all matching subgroups unbounded (-1, -1) before client-side permission filtering and pagination, causing under-filled/empty pages and evaluating every subgroup per page request

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResource.getSubGroups(), the stream is filtered before being passed into paginatedStream: `group.getSubGroupsStream(..., -1, -1).filter(auth.groups()::canView), first, max)`. This means pagination is applied after permission filtering, so the claim about under-filled/empty pages due to client-side filtering is not supported by the diff. Also, the unbounded `(-1, -1)` call was already present before this change; the diff mainly simplifies the filter predicate, not introducing a new behavior of fetching everything eagerly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission result is not cached per request/session (GroupPermissions.java:298+ / GroupPermissionsV2.java:104), unlike MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() which caches its evaluator; a single admin UI page load calls both UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount, doubling the full realm group scan and per-group policy evaluation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a potentially expensive `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` implementation that performs a full scan over group resources and per-group permission evaluation (`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`: `resourceStore.findByType(... GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` + `hasPermission(...)`). There is no caching of the computed ID set in either `GroupPermissions` or `GroupPermissionsV2`; only the evaluator instance is cached in `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()`. The diff also introduces multiple call sites that can invoke this method independently (e.g., `UsersResource.getUsersCount(...)` now passes `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` also calls it to set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`), so the same request flow could recompute the scan twice. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern created/exposed by the change, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Correctness concern: removal of the per-user .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) in UsersResource.searchForUser means user results are governed solely by the GROUPS attribute filter — the group-id set built from VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS resources won't reflect VIEW/MANAGE scoped group resources, and direct user-level grants are silently dropped from search results for restricted admins

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, but the finding’s conclusion that results are now governed *solely* by the `UserModel.GROUPS` attribute filter and that “direct user-level grants are silently dropped” is not verifiable from the diff. The method still passes `usersEvaluator` into `toRepresentation(...)`, whose implementation is not shown here and could still enforce per-user visibility. Also, while `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (new/renamed) indeed derives IDs based on member-related scopes (VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS), the claim that it *should* reflect group VIEW/MANAGE scopes is an expectation/semantics assertion not established by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of post-search canView filter in UsersResource.java:445–452 (searchForUser) means callers lacking users().canView() with empty groupIds trigger unrestricted searchForUserStream, returning every user in the realm to an unauthorized admin at GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users; same latent exposure in BruteForceUsersResource.java:147–153

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource#searchForUser`, the diff removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` on the result of `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and now directly passes the raw stream into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction mechanism in this method is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty; when that set is empty (e.g., a caller can query users but has no view permission on any groups), no filtering occurs in this method and the backend search call is no longer post-filtered by `canView`, which can expose users that the evaluator would otherwise deny. The finding’s claim about BruteForceUsersResource being a newly introduced issue is less supported (it already lacked a `canView` filter before), but the removal in `UsersResource` is a concrete security regression in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 46–53) grants manage permission from the VIEW scope via hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), violating the documented MANAGE-only contract on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() and enabling privilege escalation on group create/update/delete paths

Breaking public SPI/interface surface: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) deleted from the interface and its impl removed from GroupPermissions.java:298–311, with getGroupsWithViewPermission() renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: `GroupPermissionEvaluator` removes `boolean getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group);` and replaces `Set<String> getGroupsWithViewPermission();` with `Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (see interface changes). Correspondingly, `GroupPermissions` deletes both implementations of `getGroupsWithViewPermission(...)` and adds `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (around the shown removal/addition). This is a concrete, breaking change to a public Java interface surface (any external callers/implementers will no longer compile), but it is not inherently a runtime correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking public API: UserPermissions public canManageDefault() and canViewDefault() methods deleted (also removed from RolePermissions.canMapRole call site, confirming external usage existed)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete two previously `public` methods on `UserPermissions`: `canManageDefault()` (removed around services/.../UserPermissions.java @@-177) and `canViewDefault()` (removed at the end of the file). That is a source/binary-incompatible change for any external code calling those methods. However, the finding’s claim that “external usage existed” is not verifiable from this diff; the only confirmed call-site change shown is internal (`RolePermissions.canMapRole` no longer calls `root.users().canManageDefault()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking public API: ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...) deleted, a public static utility in server-spi-private used by extensions, with no deprecation cycle and binary compatibility breaks (NoSuchMethodError)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes the public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` from `server-spi-private` (see removal in `ModelToRepresentation.java`). That is a binary-incompatible change for any external code compiled against the old signature (would cause `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime). This is a concrete API/compatibility concern rather than an in-repo functional defect, and the diff does not show any deprecation bridge or replacement method kept for compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds the authorization resource's ID (groupResource.getId()) to the granted set, but hasPermission looks resources up by name; unless resources are created with id == groupId, the UserModel.GROUPS attribute contains resource UUIDs instead of group IDs so the user-search store filter matches nothing and group-scoped admins see no users

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates authorization resources by type and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set, and also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` (new file `GroupPermissionsV2.java`). However `hasPermission` looks up a resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, i.e., it expects a *group id / resource name*, not the authz resource UUID. Separately, callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser`, `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`, and `UsersResource.getUsersCount`) now set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` using `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, which by naming/usage is intended to be actual group IDs for user-store filtering. Returning authz resource UUIDs (and checking permissions by UUID-as-name) would cause mismatches and can result in group-scoped admins not seeing users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Scope drift between canView(group) (satisfied by VIEW/MANAGE scopes) and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (collects only VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS), so an admin granted view on a group sees the group resource but its member users don't appear in user search results

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally separates group visibility from visibility of group members: GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) is satisfied by VIEW/MANAGE on the group, while getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (used to scope user searches via session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)) collects groups where the caller has VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS. This matches the new permission model and is reinforced by the added test GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest which asserts users become visible only after granting VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS, not VIEW. So “admin with VIEW on a group should see its member users in user search” is not supported by the diff’s intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getOrCreateResource in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (~105–112) now throws IllegalStateException for unknown resource types where it previously fell through with null name and hit null-handling, causing 500s for callers/extensions passing custom or future resource types

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, the diff replaces the old if/else resolution (which left `name` as null for unknown `resourceType` and then relied on later `if (name == null)` handling) with a `switch` that has a `default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Resource type [...] not found.")`. This is a concrete behavior change: callers passing a resourceType not in {Clients, Groups, Users} will now get an unchecked exception (likely propagating as a 500) rather than whatever the prior null-path did. The finding's claim that the old behavior "caus[ed] 500s" is not verifiable from the shown diff, but the new throw for unknown types is real and could be a compatibility/robustness concern for extensions/future types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener (AdminPermissions.java:71–98) moved the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check from inside the listener to around manager.register(...), so a listener registered while the feature was off never cleans up group resources when the feature is later enabled, leaving stale permission resources

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change semantics: `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now registers the `ProviderEventListener` only if `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is true at registration time, whereas before it always registered and gated behavior inside `onEvent` (AdminPermissions.java). If the feature flag could ever become enabled later in the same runtime (without re-invoking `registerListener`), the cleanup logic in `onEvent` (e.g., disabling permissions on removed groups/roles) would never run because no listener was registered. Whether runtime toggling is supported isn’t verifiable from the diff, so this is a diff-grounded edge-case/behavior-change concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed per-user canView filter in UsersResource.searchForUser combined with getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returning an empty set in both 'global view' and 'no view permission' cases, so the GROUPS session attribute is never set and searchForUserStream runs unrestricted, leaking the full user list to admins with zero view permissions

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-user permission filter: it used to do `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` but now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` directly to `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time it relies on setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` only when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. However, `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` explicitly returns `Collections.emptySet()` when `root.users().canView()` (global view) AND also returns `Collections.emptySet()` in various “no applicable permission” cases (e.g., not same realm, no resource server, or no matching group permissions). This means callers without global user-view and without any group member-view permission will not get the GROUPS restriction applied and will no longer be filtered by `usersEvaluator::canView`, potentially exposing unrestricted search results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as satisfying manage (falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), granting write/manage access to admins with only read-only view grants — privilege escalation
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly treats VIEW as sufficient for manage by falling back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), enabling users with only VIEW to gain manage/write access. This is the same issue described in the golden comment (canManage should require only MANAGE, while canView can allow VIEW or MANAGE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: registerListener ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved from per-event to registration time; if Profile is not yet resolved during early bootstrap the cleanup listener is never registered, leaking stale group/role permission resources

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`: previously the listener was always registered and gated on `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)` per-event; now it only registers the listener if the feature is enabled at registration time. If the feature-enable decision could differ later (e.g., initialization order/late profile resolution), the cleanup logic for `RoleRemovedEvent` / `GroupRemovedEvent` would never run. However, the claim about “early bootstrap” and definite resource leakage is not verifiable from the diff alone, so this is a risk/architecture concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupResource and GroupsResource causes full per-group policy evaluation for every group in the stream even for admins with global view, turning O(1) into O(n) authz evaluations — performance regression

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResource.getSubGroups and GroupsResource.getGroups the diff removes the `canViewGlobal` boolean short-circuit (`canView()` computed once) and replaces the predicate with `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` / `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`. For callers who have global view via a realm-wide permission (e.g., V2 `GroupPermissionsV2.canView()` uses `hasPermission(null, ...)`), the old code would avoid calling `canView(group)` per element, while the new code forces a per-group `canView(group)` evaluation that may hit `resourceStore.findByName(...)` and permission evaluation for each group. This is a concrete performance regression risk, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes while canView(group) accepts VIEW/MANAGE, causing inconsistent results: admins granted VIEW can open a group page but user searches scoped by GROUPS return no members, and counts disagree across endpoints

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group)` checks group-scopes `VIEW/MANAGE`, while `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` collects groups where the caller has `VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS` (used by `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` to scope user search/count). However, the diff does not establish that this is inconsistent or incorrect: it is plausible and consistent with the surrounding changes that “viewing a group” is distinct from “viewing group members/users”, and user search scoping should be driven by member-view scopes, not group-view scopes. The claimed broken behavior (UI can open group page but cannot see members; counts disagree) is not verifiable from the diff alone and assumes a permission model not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse can NPE on 201 responses without a Location header (or when assertion framework continues on failure), producing a less diagnosable error in test infrastructure

adjudication.rationale: In `ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse`, the new implementation still unconditionally dereferences `response.getLocation().getPath()`. If a 201 response lacks a `Location` header, `response.getLocation()` can be `null`, causing an immediate NPE in this helper (same risk existed before, but the method is modified in this diff and the defect remains verifiable from the code shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of defensive in-stream permission filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource.java:455 and BruteForceUsersResource.java:~147 is untested; if a user federation/provider ignores the GROUPS session attribute, a group-scoped admin silently sees all users

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser(), the explicit defensive authorization gate `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed and the stream is now passed directly to `toRepresentation(...)` (diff around UsersResource.java:446-455). BruteForceUsersResource similarly now passes `searchForUserStream(...)` directly after only setting `UserModel.GROUPS` in the session (BruteForceUsersResource.java ~144-151). The only remaining restriction shown in the diff is setting a session attribute with group IDs (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`), which is an indirect constraint dependent on the underlying user provider honoring that session attribute. If a federation/provider ignores it, the REST layer no longer enforces `usersEvaluator.canView(user)` and can return users outside the admin’s group-scoped visibility, i.e., a permission/visibility regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V1 semantics change in GroupPermissions.java:298 — guard now checks only canView() instead of canView() || canManage(), so admins with MANAGE_USERS but not VIEW_USERS now get a non-empty group set; no V1 test covers this

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the guard changed from `if (root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage())` to `if (root.users().canView())`. But per the diff, `UserPermissions.canView()` now returns true when the caller has `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` (it checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`), so an admin with MANAGE_USERS but not VIEW_USERS will still hit the `canView()` short-circuit and get an empty set. The finding’s claimed behavior change (non-empty set for MANAGE_USERS-only) is not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.java:74 — ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved to registration time, so listener is never registered if the feature is toggled on after registration; untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check from inside the listener callback to wrapping the `manager.register(...)` call (AdminPermissions.java). However, the finding’s claimed defect depends on the feature being “toggled on after registration”. Nothing in the diff indicates that Keycloak profile features are dynamically toggled at runtime or that `registerListener` is expected to be re-run when a feature flag changes. The statement “untested” is also not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest leaks user policies — same policy name 'Only My Admin User Policy' reused across multiple tests without cleanup, causing collisions or order-dependent results

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, multiple tests call `createUserPolicy(...)` with the same hard-coded name (`"Only My Admin User Policy"`). The `@AfterEach` cleanup only removes scope permissions via `ScopePermissionsResource` and does not remove any user policies that were created. From the diff alone we can verify the name reuse and the lack of policy cleanup, which can make tests order-dependent or cause collisions if policy names must be unique in the underlying authz store.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for GroupResource.java:177 getSubGroups pagination-with-filter interaction — filtering before pagination can return fewer-than-max results for scoped admins

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResource.getSubGroups the code passes an *unpaginated* stream (`group.getSubGroupsStream(..., -1, -1)`) through `.filter(...)` and only then applies `paginatedStream(..., first, max)`. Filtering before pagination does not inherently cause “fewer-than-max results” (it typically helps fill pages with permitted results as long as enough permitted items exist). Also, this ordering (filter then paginate) already existed before the change; the diff only simplifies the predicate from `canViewGlobal || canView(g)` to `canView(g)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BruteForceUsersResource.java:147 group-scoped brute-force user search is completely untested, duplicating UsersResource logic and prone to drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser/searchForUser(...) to mirror UsersResource logic for group-scoped visibility by setting session attribute UserModel.GROUPS from auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (and removes the prior conditional on !auth.users().canView()). This is nontrivial permission/visibility behavior duplicated across two resources and therefore prone to drift. The added/modified tests in the diff (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest, updates to RealmAdminPermissionsConfig) exercise group/user permission evaluation via Users/Groups admin endpoints, but nothing in the diff shows coverage for the BruteForceUsersResource brute-force user search endpoint specifically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:52 contains a double semicolon typo (new GroupRepresentation();;)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` in `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, but the extra semicolon is valid Java (an empty class-body declaration) and does not affect compilation or runtime behavior. It’s a minor style nit rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope and canManageMembership path added to schema have no test coverage at all

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP to the group resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema and implements GroupPermissionsV2.canManageMembership(...) using that scope. The new test class GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest includes testManageGroupMembership(), which explicitly creates a group permission with scope MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for topGroup (createGroupPermission(topGroup, Set.of(MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP), policy)) and then verifies the admin can join a user to that group. This exercises the newly added manage-membership permission path rather than leaving it untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (~line 46) global check falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing callers with only the view scope on all-groups to manage groups — a security leak and inconsistent with the per-resource canManage(group) which checks only MANAGE

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2` (file `services/.../GroupPermissionsV2.java`), `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. That means a caller with only the global (all-groups) `VIEW` scope would satisfy `canManage()` and could pass checks that rely on the global manage capability. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel group)`, which requires only `MANAGE` via `hasPermission(group.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, and suggests an unintended privilege escalation for global operations gated by `canManage()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent resource identity in GroupPermissionsV2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() collects groupResource.getId() while hasPermission(groupId, ...) resolves via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId); if resource IDs differ from group IDs, the returned set is not usable group IDs for UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource consumers

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates group resources via resourceStore.findByType(...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned Set. But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its argument as a *group id / resource name* and resolves the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Passing groupResource.getId() (authorization resource internal id) into hasPermission will not match findByName unless resource id == resource name. Additionally, the returned set is later used as group IDs (e.g., UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource set UserModel.GROUPS to these IDs), so returning authorization resource IDs would be unusable if they differ from actual group IDs. The diff does not show any guarantee that Resource.getId() equals the group id/name; AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name, suggesting the resource name is the group id and the resource id is distinct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LSP violation: GroupPermissionsV2 overrides 8 methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions, etc.) to throw UnsupportedOperationException; the GroupPermissionManagement surface should be split from the evaluator interface instead of stubbed

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `GroupPermissionsV2` extends `GroupPermissions` (which implements both `GroupPermissionEvaluator` and `GroupPermissionManagement`) but overrides multiple management-oriented methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). This is a diff-grounded contract/substitutability concern: callers obtaining `root.groups()` (now `MgmtPermissionsV2#groups()` returns `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)`) can still legally invoke the management surface but will get runtime exceptions. The finding’s suggestion to split evaluator vs management instead of stubbing is therefore actionable and grounded, though whether it manifests as an immediate runtime bug is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() logic across GroupPermissions.java and GroupPermissionsV2.java (~20-line near-identical implementations differing only in the permission-evaluation predicate); extract the skeleton into the base class with a hook

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissions` now implements `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` with a common precheck skeleton (return empty if `root.users().canView()`, then same-realm check, then `realmResourceServer()` null check, then iterating group resources to collect granted IDs). The new `GroupPermissionsV2` overrides `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and repeats the same structural logic, differing mainly in how `hasPermission(...)` is evaluated for each group resource. This is a concrete duplication introduced by the change and is a reasonable refactoring/architecture issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Widened visibility (private → protected) of root, resourceStore, policyStore fields in GroupPermissions.java:56-58 purely for subclass access, leaking store internals instead of exposing protected behavior hooks

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `GroupPermissions` fields `root`, `resourceStore`, and `policyStore` from `private` to `protected` (services/.../GroupPermissions.java), and introduces `GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions` which uses those internals (e.g., `root`, `resourceStore.findByType(...)`, `policyStore.findByResource(...)`). This is a real design/encapsulation concern created by the change: it widens the exposure of internal stores to subclasses rather than providing protected methods/hooks for the needed operations. It’s not a functional defect by itself, but it does increase coupling and leaks implementation details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resolveGroup in AdminPermissionsSchema.java:181-186 breaks the naming contract of resolveUser/resolveClient by returning group.getId() (an ID) where siblings return human-meaningful names; rename or document the divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `resolveGroup(...)` returns `group.getId()` (new method in `AdminPermissionsSchema`) and `getOrCreateResource(...)` now uses that to derive the resource `name` via a `switch`. That is a real inconsistency risk because this `resolve*` family is used to turn an internal model id into the stored resource name, and returning an id for groups may be surprising or reduce human readability in the authorization store. However, the diff alone does not prove an explicit “naming contract” nor show what `resolveUser/resolveClient` return, and other new code (e.g., `GroupPermissionsV2` using `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`) suggests using the group id as the name may be intentional. So this is a specific, diff-grounded maintainability/consistency concern rather than a verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated 'GROUPS session attribute' pre-search logic: UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser contain byte-for-byte identical blocks (getGroupIdsWithViewPermission → setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS) → toRepresentation); should live in one shared helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same new pre-search block added in both BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...) and UsersResource.searchForUser(...): it computes `Set<String> groupIds = auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission();` and, if non-empty, sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds);` before calling `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and `toRepresentation(...)`. This is a real duplication/maintainability concern introduced/solidified by the change, but it is not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` silently removed from UsersResource.searchForUser; admins with QUERY_USERS but no VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS role and empty groupIds get no GROUPS attribute set, so search returns every user in the realm

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the explicit per-user authorization gate: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is changed to `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` with no subsequent filter. At the same time, `UserModel.GROUPS` is only set when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty; for callers who can query but lack global view/manage and have no group-based view permissions, `groupIds` will be empty and no session restriction is applied. From the diff alone, there is no other shown safeguard in this method to prevent returning users the caller cannot view, so the removal constitutes a real authorization/correctness regression risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly passes when admin has only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource, allowing view-only admins to pass requireManage() and create/update groups

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `hasPermission(null, ...)` falls back to the resource-type (“all-groups”) resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) and checks whether *any* of the provided scopes are granted, an admin granted only the `VIEW` scope on the all-groups resource will make `canManage()` return `true`. Since `requireManage()` in `GroupPermissions` is implemented as `if (!canManage()) throw new ForbiddenException();`, this would allow view-only all-groups permissions to satisfy `requireManage()` and thus potentially allow create/update operations that rely on it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds authz resource IDs instead of group IDs (group ID is stored as resource name), causing user search/count to silently return zero users for admins with legitimate VIEW_MEMBERS permissions

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, it iterates `resourceStore.findByType(... GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` and, on success, adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set and also calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource()` resolves the *resource name* for groups via `resolveGroup()` returning `group.getId()`, meaning the group ID is stored as the authorization resource **name**, while `Resource#getId()` is the internal authz resource identifier. `hasPermission()` then does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, so passing `groupResource.getId()` (internal id) will not match the resource name (group id), causing the permission check to fail and the returned set to contain the wrong identifiers. Since callers (e.g., `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource`) now pass this set as `UserModel.GROUPS` filtering input, this can incorrectly filter out users (silently returning 0).

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() only scans per-group resources and ignores grants on the typed all-groups resource, inconsistent with canViewMembers(group) which honors the all-groups fallback

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates authorization Resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), then adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. However hasPermission() expects a *group id / resource name* (it does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), whereas Resource.getId() is the internal authz resource id, not the group id. This means per-group resources likely won’t be found by name, causing fallback evaluation against the typed all-groups resource, and even when granted it returns a set of authz resource IDs (and/or only the typed resource) rather than actual group IDs. As a result, callers that set session attribute UserModel.GROUPS with this set (e.g., UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) will not properly restrict/allow user search by group ids, and all-groups grants are not translated into appropriate group-id sets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission creates persisted authorization resources on read paths via getOrCreateResource, causing read-only requests to mutate state and risking ModelDuplicateException races on concurrent first requests

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` only reading from stores (`resourceStore.findByName`, `policyStore.findByResource`) and, on miss, falling back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. There is no call to `getOrCreateResource` (nor any other explicit create/persist operation) in `GroupPermissionsV2` in this diff, so the claim that it “creates persisted authorization resources on read paths via getOrCreateResource” is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature-gate check for ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ moved from per-event evaluation in onEvent to registration time, so enabling the feature after startup leaves the cleanup listener unregistered and orphaned authz resources accumulate

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener` the diff changes from always registering a `ProviderEventListener` and checking `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` inside `onEvent(...)` to only registering the listener when the feature is enabled at registration time (`if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { manager.register(...) }`). This is a real behavioral change: if the feature flag were to become enabled after `registerListener` has already run, events would no longer be observed because the listener was never registered. The diff itself does not establish whether Keycloak profile features can change at runtime, so the claimed “orphaned authz resources accumulate” outcome is not directly verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupResource.getSubGroups and GroupsResource.getGroups causes a per-group permission evaluation on every listing, a performance regression for admins with global view rights

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the cached `canViewGlobal` boolean and replaces `filter(g -> canViewGlobal || ...canView(g))` with `filter(...::canView)` in both `GroupResource.getSubGroups` and `GroupsResource.getGroups`. This means `canView(GroupModel)` is invoked for every returned group during listing. For callers with global view rights, this previously short-circuited after a single `canView()` check; now it does repeated checks per group. This can be particularly expensive under the new V2 evaluator (`GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)`), which (when not covered by admin roles) runs a permission evaluation for each group ID rather than relying on a one-time global `canView()` evaluation (which would check the resource-type “all-groups” permission once). This is a diff-grounded performance concern, not a correctness defect.
